Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
255 PM EDT Sat Aug 29 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 255 PM EDT Saturday...

No significant changes made with this forecast package.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 255 PM EDT Saturday...

1. Showers and embedded rumbles expected Sunday and again on 
Tuesday, but the probability of highly impactful or significant 
weather is less than 5% at this time. 

2. A period of showery weather is expected mid to late week, 
with a emphasis on Wednesday night into Thursday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 255 PM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Water vapor imagery shows deep dry layer associated with 
high pres both aloft and at the sfc wl cont to shift east of our cwa 
tonight, as llvl waa develops on increasing south/southwest flow. 
The combination of warm and moisture advection, along with a weak 
embedded disturbance over the northern Great Lakes and associated 
pocket of mid lvl moisture wl approach our International Border area 
overnight with a 30-40% probability of showers. Upstream radar does 
indicate some scattered activity angling toward our northern zones 
tonight. In addition, 925mb to 850mb south to southwest winds 
increase 30 to 40 knots overnight, which combined with some mid lvl 
clouds wl limit fog development, maybe some patchy fog in the CT 
River Valley. Temps with better mixing and some mid lvl clouds hold 
in the upper 40s NEK to lower 60s parts of the CPV. 

Sunday-Sunday night fcst focus wl be timing and areal coverage of 
showers with a rumble of thunder. Latest trends continue to support 
highest 60-75% pops acrs the northern Dacks into northern/central 
mtns of VT on Sunday with 15 to 30% over southern areas. HREF 
indicates 60 to 80% prob of QPF >0.10" near the International 
Border, while only 10-30% prob over central-southern VT on Sunday. 
HREF suggested 40-60% of QPF >0.25 northern sections and <15% over 
southern areas, highlighting the north to south precip gradient 
expected and the associated pop configuration. The RRFS mean QPF is 
btwn 0.10" to 0.25" north to <0.05" south. Little has changed in the 
overall synoptic setup with embedded 700-500mb vorticity in the fast 
confluent flow aloft riding along a sfc cold frnt dropping 
southward, while best instability and deeper moisture is displaced 
to our south. As flow becomes northerly behind the boundary with 
lingering 200-400 J/kg of CAPE and moisture thru 700mb, feel a 
period of favorable conditions for upslope rain showers are likely 
btwn 00z-04z Monday. Have used the upslope climo tool to highlight 
this potential in the grids, which could include the eastern CPV 
associated with developing blocked flow. After midnight sounding 
data indicates a sharpening and lowering subsidence inversion with 
moisture trapped below 900mb, supporting areas of low stratus clouds 
and fog, especially in favorable upslope regions/mtns with more fog 
possible in the deeper valleys. Could be widespread based on latest 
trends. Highs Manley in the 70s again on Sunday with lows upper 40s 
to upper 50s by Monday morning. By Monday, a very dry airmass is 
overhead with PW values <0.50, but lingering low clouds/fog could 
prevail thru 10 AM based on sounding data. Once the clouds burn off 
a beautiful day withe plenty of sunshine and comfortable temps are 
expected.

Monday night and Tuesday...Pattern begins to shift again as strong 
mid/upper lvl ridge tries to expand northeast toward our cwa, while 
closed cyclonic circulation remains anchored over eastern Canada. 
This produces a fast confluent flow aloft with a sharpening 
southwest to northeast temps/moisture gradient over the Mid 
Atlantic/NE CONUS. As short wave energy aloft rides along this 
strengthening llvl boundary an area of moderate rain with embedded 
heavier thunderstorms is likely. However, placement of this activity 
and associated axis of heaviest precip has a very low predictability 
at this time, given large spread in guidance. Latest guidance shows 
best instability progs along and south of a Watertown to Albany 
line, which would be a favorable track for cluster of showers with 
embedded thunderstorms. NBM shows 60-70% prob of QPF>0.25" south of 
a MSS to BTV to LEB with just 20 to 35% over the NEK. The 25th 
percentile is 0.10", while the 75th is 1.0" with mean values btwn 
0.25 to 0.75" mostly south of MSS to BTV to LEB line on Tuesday. For 
now have gone with NBM with highest pops acrs our southern cwa and 
less over the NEK of VT. Highs stay near seasonable levels.

KEY MESSAGE 2: During the middle and end of the week, an upper level 
trough will gradually shunt a ridge over the Midwest and Mid-
Atlantic to the south, preventing any heat from building into the 
region. The last of a couple ridge runner type features will move 
through Wednesday night into Thursday, likely bringing an area of 
heavy rain with convective enhancement from elevated instability. 
The warm sector will not be fully established over the area so 
limited surface instability should limit the threat for severe 
weather. However, increasing PWATs and good dynamics will cause an 
axis of heavy rain to develop, though its exact placement is 
uncertain. The flood threat looks low at this point but will 
continue to be watched. For any flash flooding to occur, the band on 
Wednesday night into Thursday would likely have to occur in the 
exact location as the heavier bands in the beginning of the week for 
a chance. NBM probabilities of 2+ inches of rain are up to around 20 
percent for southern Vermont, the part of the region that has the 
highest probability of seeing the heaviest rain. Surface high 
pressure gradually builds into the region for late week and next 
weekend, and it is potentially shaping up to be another winner of a 
weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 18Z Sunday...VFR conditions will prevail through almost the
entire next 24 hours. The exception will be tomorrow morning when
some scattered showers should move through MSS, potentially dropping
the visibility to MVFR for a brief period of time. However, thunder
is not expected. Southerly winds will prevail this afternoon,
generally between 5-15 KT. Winds become more westerly tonight and
could gust up to 20 KT at MSS. LLWS will develop at most terminals
this evening and will continue for most of the night, but it should
end by 12Z. Isolated to scattered showers with a couple embedded
thunderstorms will move through tomorrow afternoon, which could
cause brief visibility reductions to MVFR/IFR and erratic winds.

Outlook...

Sunday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Monday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday: Mainly IFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 255 PM EDT Saturday...

Have issued Lake Wind Advisory for tonight, based on increasing 
south to southwest winds 15 to 25 knots, especially the broad/open 
waters around midnight tonight. Given the warm water temps helping 
to increase mixing heights, feel as low level jet of 20 to 25 knots 
develops with channeled southerly flow, a few gusts up to 25 knots 
will be likely overnight on Lake Champlain. Wave will build 1 to 3 
feet overnight into Sunday morning.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
